why: harbor_master's charter states its own falsifier: 'if devices advance workflows AROUND it once the clearance gate lands (ambient transitions), the authority rung has failed (Law 6).' The clearance gate landed 2026-07-21 (child b) and the fourth refusal 2026-08-04. Measured 2026-08-05: of 229 records across 21 component histories, 146 are emit-shaped and ZERO carry cleared_by. Not one crossing in the system's whole recorded life has passed the authority rung. The condition the component named as its own falsification is met, and has been met continuously since the gate was built. The lived symptom: read cairn/tools/base/transitions.py:70 and you are told 'the clearance gate wraps emit, so this is the one door' — three files say it — and then any caller imports emit and moves a boat's cursor, which is exactly what every crossing on disk did.

occurrences.location: cairn/devices/harbor_master/clearance.py:170 (clear); cairn/tools/base/transitions.py:732 (emit) and :844 (the projector append that writes the record of truth); the 21 history.json files under cairn/

occurrences.expected: A journaled crossing reaches projector.append_entry only through clear(), so every record of truth carries cleared_by and every cursor move was checked against Law 6 (authority), Law 8 (proven method) and the harbor's resource lines before it was written.
occurrences.actual: 229 records; 146 emit-shaped (direction+workflow present); 0 with cleared_by. Distribution of the emit-shaped ones: chart 47, build_inspector 42, librarian 22, orient 12, learning_block 10, base 9, intention_extractor 3, intentions_model_compiler 1. grep across the repo finds NO production caller of clear() — every call site is in cairn/devices/harbor_master/proofs/test_clearance.py — and no production .py caller of emit() either: the 146 crossings were made by CC invoking emit inline, which is the ambient advance the rung exists to stop.
occurrences.how_measured: python3 — walk cairn/**/history.json, count records, count those carrying both 'direction' and 'workflow' (emit's own record shape, transitions.py:807-843), count those carrying 'cleared_by' (written only by clear(), clearance.py:256). Plus grep for callers of clear( and of cairn.tools.base.transitions across the repo, excluding proofs. Re-runnable; reads only committed files. Registry half: grep for '.resolve(' across the repo (one production consumer, return value unused); read harbor_master filed_edges (a) for a planned consumer (none); count find . -path '*/validations/*.json' (73); grep read_validations/validations_path_for outside cairn/devices/tester (0 readers); grep 'horizon' for an expiry check anywhere outside the tester's own writer (none).
occurrences.fatality: non-fatal and silent, which is the shape of it. Every crossing was made by the box's one owner, so nothing wrong has actually been authorized — the records are true. What is false is the claim, restated in three files, that a gate stands between a caller and a record of truth. A reader of transitions.py:70 today is told there is one door, and there are two.
occurrences.what_it_blocks: Admission control cannot run anywhere. The fourth refusal (Unresourced) is built, proven, and — as of this trouble's sibling proof, cairn/devices/harbor_master/proofs/test_harbor_asks_the_real_host.py — proven against the REAL system_rackmount device in both directions. It still never fires, because the function it lives in is never called. Wiring resources= is not the missing step; a caller is.
occurrences.the_two_dispositions: FIX NOW is not available: making clear() the only door needs an answer to what a crossing's actor, boat_owner and method ARE for the crossings we actually make (today the mover is CC and the 'method' a PROVED crossing summons is arguably the component's own proof), and the MethodRegistry is in-memory with no production register() call, so every crossing would re-run a proof under the tester. That is a stone, not an edit. TICKET, therefore — and the ticket's first question is whether emit's journal path should refuse a crossing that carries no cleared_by. Note the threat model clearance.py:32 declares for itself: 'Forgery is not the threat model on a single-owner cooperative box; AMBIENT authority is.' Under that model a required, explicit cleared_by IS sufficient physics — it makes accidental bypass impossible, and deliberate lying is out of scope by the component's own charter. Blast radius measured: 36 emit call sites pass history_path, 35 of them in proofs (test_transitions 30, test_clearance 9 via clear, test_v2_migration 4, test_watchme_vocabulary 1, test_emission_gate 1). SHARPENED 2026-08-05 (Akien: 'methodregistry is a registry. generally we frown on registries. why do we need one here?') — we do not, and the blocker above dissolves with it. MEASURED: clearance.py:233 is the registry's ONLY consumer and it DISCARDS the returned callable, so the one thing a registry uniquely provides (name -> object) serves nobody; filed_edges names no future consumer for it either. The fact it caches already lives at a DERIVED address — validations_path_for(proof_path) maps proofs/x.py -> validations/x.json, 73 trails on disk — so there is nothing to look up: the proof's address is the key, and the registry is a second in-memory copy of a record that already attaches at its own endpoint (the manager smell, Law 6). The copy is also WEAKER: a VALIDATION carries `horizon` ('valid until the proof file or the code it proves changes'), a registry entry carries none and resolve() does no expiry check, so a registry populated at wiring time keeps answering green after the code moves under it (Law 8 wants the seal, not the cache). PROVENANCE explains the presence: registry.py's own header says 'RE-INSTATED, NOT RE-DERIVED (Law 1)' — it came back from the ground_loop driver-executor, which DISPATCHED and so genuinely needed name->callable; that executor role was called a goof and stripped, and the registry returned with its map intact and its consumer changed. Law 1 forbids re-deriving a settled answer; it does not license carrying one forward when the question moved. HONEST COST: those 73 trails have ZERO readers today, so 'resolve against the seal' is new machinery, not existing machinery — but the reader is wanted anyway (the horizon check, and Law 9's green-is-earned both need exactly it), and it replaces a wiring-time proof re-run with a file read.

found_by: working item 1 of the extant build order ('wire the gate' — the slate's read was that nothing passes resources= to clear()). Verifying that read before acting on it found the larger fact underneath: nothing passes ANYTHING to clear(). The slate's stated blocker — 'wiring needs a live system_rackmount instance the harbor can reach' — is also measured false: ask() is a plain method on the device, no bus, no daemon, no instance (proven in test_harbor_asks_the_real_host.py).
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy — 'the one door' is prose in three files and physics in none)
Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner; the owner alone gates writes to it)
Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — 0 of 229 is the whole content of this trouble)
Law 9 (red is the default; a component whose falsifier is met reads green because nothing derives red)
filed_edges: [AKIEN] IS CLEARANCE MANDATORY OR ADVISORY? harbor_master's own falsifier reads as mandatory — 'if devices advance workflows AROUND it once the clearance gate lands, the authority rung has failed (Law 6)' — and 229 records say every crossing goes around it. So either the gate is advisory and that falsifier is wrong, or it is mandatory and the chokepoint must refuse an uncleared crossing (Law 4). This is not a bug to fix but a ruling to make, because 'mandatory' changes every crossing path that exists.

[CORPUS] IF MANDATORY, WHAT IS THE BOOTSTRAP? The gate itself has to be crossed into existence, and the first crossing cannot be cleared by a gate that is not yet running. Whatever the answer, it should be a NAMED exemption in a roster, not an accident of ordering — same roster question a-voyage-names-its-ticket is already asking.

drained_to.why: troubles/ is a pre-ticket inbox, not a parallel place work lives; a trouble that never becomes a ticket is a bug with no workflow (ruling 2026-08-02-three-entry-points-and-structural-refiled). This trouble was the last un-drained one in the store — it carried two [AKIEN] filed_edges for five days and had no workflow at all, which is the exact shape that ruling names. THIS RECORD STAYS: it is the account of the live symptom; the ticket is what moves through the gates. STANDING DOES NOT CHANGE HERE — the trouble clears when the work does, and the work is a stone Akien explicitly scoped as 'cast it as a ticket, not build it now'.
drained_to.the_akien_edges_are_answered: Filed edge one, IS CLEARANCE MANDATORY OR ADVISORY — RULED MANDATORY 2026-08-10. The falsifier stands as written and the code moves to meet it. Filed edge two, IF MANDATORY WHAT IS THE BOOTSTRAP — carried into the ticket as child (b), the-bootstrap-is-a-named-roster, with this trouble's own requirement preserved: a NAMED exemption in a roster, not an accident of ordering.
drained_to.re_measured_at_drain: 2026-08-10: 186 emit-shaped records of 280 total across the component histories, ZERO carrying cleared_by (was 146 of 229 on 2026-08-05 — the gap GREW by 40, four of them added by CC during the session that re-measured it). Still no production caller of clear(): every call site remains in cairn/devices/harbor_master/proofs/test_clearance.py.
drained_to.conformance_taken_now: The ruling's immediate half did not wait for the build. The four present-tense sites in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py claiming 'the clearance gate wraps emit' now say it does not and name the ticket; harbor_master's charter records that its falsifier is MET and retracts how_it_learns' claim that the learning precondition was satisfied. So the trouble's sharpest complaint — that a reader of transitions.py:70 is told there is one door when there are two — is FIXED TODAY, even though the gate itself is not.

cleared_by.what_changed: THE SIXTH SEAT LANDED AND THE CORPUS COUNT MOVED OFF ZERO. cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit now refuses a forward journaled crossing INTO A REST that carries no cleared_by (ClearanceRequiredRed, raised before the record dict is assembled, nothing written), and the witness is RE-READ AGAINST THE WORLD — an incomplete witness, a proof the tester never sealed, and a seal date disagreeing with standing() each refuse in their own words, so a hand-typed cleared_by forges nothing. Measured at the close: 2 of 193 emit-shaped records carry cleared_by, both this voyage own (cairn/tools/base/history.json seq 35 and 36); every prior denominator taken of this corpus read ZERO (0 of 146 here, 0 of 186 at cast, 0 of 189 at survey). The PROVED crossing at seq 36 is in the demanded set and CLEARED rather than being waived — _CLEARANCE_EXEMPT_ROSTER is empty in production. THE CAUSE THIS TROUBLE COULD NOT SEE: clear() was structurally UNCALLABLE since 2026-07-29 (three gates inside emit read journal_extra[ticket] and clear() accepted none), so the year of ambient crossings was physics pointing the wrong way, not indiscipline. The three files that said the gate WRAPPED emit are corrected with their superseded words kept: it is a SEAT AT that door. RESIDUE, NAMED AND TICKETED: crossings into a SUMMONS are outside the demanded set by design; and the authority half binds only an honest caller until boat_owner is read from the boat (ticket boat_owner-is-read-not-stated).
